The campaign in the East became the second front of the war for Britain, and the Western Front was held with what the Eastern one left over. When the end came it was in France, as it was always going to be, and the armies that finished it were smaller than they might have been.-9MANPOWER ▾-5MUNITIONS ▾+3POLITICAL CAPITAL ▾Speculative counterfactualSpeculative. The Cabinet voted to evacuate Gallipoli, and did so with very small loss. What actually happened: the evacuation of Anzac and Suvla was completed on 20 December 1915 and of Helles on 8 and 9 January 1916, after which the troops went to Egypt and to France. The Gallipoli campaign cost about a quarter of a million casualties on each side, and the argument about whether another strategy could have succeeded began in 1915 and is not settled. The argument between the men who wanted to win the war in France and those who wanted a different front was never settled by the result. Churchill and Lloyd George held the second view and Robertson and Haig the first, and both sides could point to something that supported them.Your commandColonel58 out of 100Standing at the close: the three meters together stood at -1110/30The ending: an ending near the record
